what: The project-own contract set per benchmark, PINNED.
why: collect.py used to derive this by scanning a checked-out copy of each
it keyed on FILE STEMS: a contract counted as project-own iff some own
.sol file was named after it.  Those trees no longer exist, and with the
scan returning an empty set the collector silently excluded EVERY contract
in the flat -- including the primary -- and reported 0% for a run that
verified nothing.  Pinning the set here makes the pipeline self-contained
and makes a re-collection differ from the locked baseline in exactly one
provenance: Recovered verbatim from the locked notes/coverage/data/esbmc_<bench>.json:
own = (top-level contracts declared in the flat) minus (every name passed
to --coverage-exclude-contract in that file's per_function commandUsed
strings).  Reproduced for all six benchmarks; see the deviation below.
limit_order_protocol carries no exclude flags at all -- a pure-library
primary is routed through --function, which never emits them -- so its
entry is the single declared library.

detail: BalanceLib is declared in aqua's OWN src/libs/Balance.sol.  The file-stem
rule missed it (stem 'Balance' != contract 'BalanceLib'), so the locked
run excluded it from instrumentation.  The flat's `// File` marker rule --
which collect.py already uses for the DENOMINATOR and for Pair 2's
callable enumeration, and which the path-coverage collector uses
throughout -- accepts it.  The set below keeps the LOCKED answer, so that
a re-collection measures the esbmc change and nothing else.
Numerically the difference is inert: src/libs/Balance.sol contributes 0
canonical decisions (aqua's ownFilesInScope is src/Aqua.sol alone), Pair 1
skips libraries when choosing focused runs, and Pair 2 already runs
BalanceLib.load / BalanceLib.store off the marker rule -- both appear in
